subject: Clarifying regional routing guarantees, transient sync windows, and DPA steps
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@finedgepayments.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt O'Connell <matt.oconnell@finedgepayments.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Data routing commitments and temporary cross-region processing windows

Rafael —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we get procurement moving, legal and IT have a couple of specific asks around residency guarantees and any temporary cross-region processing that might occur during normal operations or recovery. High-level questions: 

- Can you confirm that inference requests and primary logs for a pinned EU deployment will remain within EU data centers for the live inference path?
- Do you perform any cross-region processing (e.g., async backups, cache warmups, model updates) that could touch customer data outside the pinned region? If so, what are the maximum windows and controls?
- How does KMS behave for pinned deployments — are keys region-bound or can transient keys be staged outside the EU?
- Please provide your current subprocessors for EU region and a timeline for any planned additions in the next 90 days.
- What level of contractual commitment can Redwood provide in the DPA? We need language that covers transient processing for disaster recovery with explicit maximum durations and notification obligations.

Matt and I are trying to scope the DPA addendum and the implementation plan. If you can share a short written response and a proposed timeline, that will speed up legal review. Also: any SOC2 or audit artifacts are appreciated.

Best,
Sara Lim
Senior Security Manager
FinEdge Payments

[Attachment requested: SOC2 Type II summary]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@finedgepayments.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data routing commitments and temporary cross-region processing windows

Sara —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; I’ve attached a short implementation timeline for the EU pin and a preliminary DPA addendum we typically propose for customers with residency needs. Marissa (legal) will provide the formal redlines, but this should give your team something concrete to review.

1) Live inference and primary request path: Yes — when a deployment is pinned to EU, the inference runtime, request routing, and primary request logs (request IDs, timing, and non-pii telemetry used for billing) are processed within EU region data centers only. We provide region-bound KMS keys for customer-managed keys when customers choose that option.

2) Cross-region processing: We do run a small set of background activities that may touch encrypted blobs for operational reasons (replication backfills, model cache warmups, and rare node rebalancing). For pinned deployments we limit this to two categories: 
   - transient operational work (e.g., cache syncs, node rebuilds): typical window is under 24 hours and we aim for less than 6 hours; the absolute maximum (for extreme cases) is 72 hours and requires an internal escalation.
   - controlled failover/backfill (disaster recovery or planned maintenance): we can allow up to 72 hours of temporary cross-region processing but only under either (a) explicit contractual allowance in the DPA, or (b) a customer-initiated failover request.

All cross-region touches occur only to encrypted payloads. For customer-managed KMS, keys remain region-bound and never leave the EU. For Redwood-managed keys, we use ephemeral key wrapping — the plaintext decryption envelope never leaves the pinned region; any temporary key material used for orchestration is auditable and limited in scope.

3) Subprocessors: I’ve attached our current EU subprocessor roster (names + roles). We do quarterly updates; I can commit to 30 days’ advance notice and the option to review or object to new subprocessors on a narrow set of legal bases (as outlined in the draft DPA).

4) DPA language: We can include explicit maximum transient windows, notification obligations within 24 hours for any non-routine cross-region touches, and a right to audit logs for such events. Marissa will propose the exact clause text (I’ve looped in legal).

Next steps:
- I’ll have Marissa send a DPA redline with the clause text and a DocuSign-ready version.
- Grace from CS will coordinate an implementation plan and target dates; the attached timeline shows a typical 4–6 week plan for EU pin (pilot -> staging -> production) assuming procurement is done.

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call with your security and infra teams next week to walk through the KMS and network controls.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
redwood.com

[Attachments: implementation-timeline-Redwood-FinEdge.xlsx, redwood-dpa-addendum-draft-v1.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@finedgepayments.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Data routing commitments and temporary cross-region processing windows — DPA redline and subprocessor roster

Sara —

Following Rafael’s note, attached is a redline of the DPA addendum that inserts: (1) a definition for "transient cross-region processing", (2) maximum duration of 72 hours for disaster recovery events with required customer notification within 24 hours of the start of processing, and (3) an advance notice period of 30 days for routine subprocessor additions with narrow objection rights. 

Key points for your team to review: 
- We can offer region-bound KMS for customer-managed keys; for Redwood-managed keys we’ve added an audit requirement and added limits on staging key material.
- For very sensitive customers we can add a dedicated tenancy option (Dedicated capacity) as an alternative; language included describes the migration path and expected timeline.

Attached: redwood-dpa-addendum-draft-v1.pdf (redline), subprocessor-roster-2026-09.csv

I’ve also prepared a DocuSign envelope (link below) with the standard addendum. If your legal team prefers to propose edits, send them back as tracked changes and we’ll review. Rafael — please confirm the implementation timeline in the spreadsheet is still accurate.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/abc123-redwood-dpa
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/FinEdge-7843

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-dpa-addendum-draft-v1.pdf, subprocessor-roster-2026-09.csv]

From: Matt O'Connell <matt.oconnell@finedgepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@finedgepayments.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data routing commitments and temporary cross-region processing windows — DPA redline and subprocessor roster

Marissa / Rafael —

Thanks for the detailed responses and the redline. The 72-hour max and 24-hour notification are both acceptable to our legal and ops teams. We’ll route the DPA addendum through our procurement queue today and expect to finish internal review by next Wednesday.

One quick question: is the 30-day notice for subprocessor additions negotiable for high-risk subprocessors (e.g., those that host analytics telemetry)? We’d like an explicit carve-out that allows us to require 60 days’ notice for subprocessors that handle non-anonymized telemetry.

Assuming we can agree on that point, we’re comfortable moving to DocuSign. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Monday to sign off and confirm the migration slots in the attached timeline?

Thanks — Matt
VP, Infrastructure
FinEdge Payments
